classification.difficultyReason: Construct overlapping event regions from totals and use them to distinguish inclusive or, neither and exactly one.

content.prompt:
Use an appropriate Venn diagram.

In a group of 65 students, 30 students study geography, 42 study history and 20 study both history and geography. If a student is chosen at random from the group of 65 students, find the probability that the student studies:

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11; completed diagram in teacher PDF page 38
spec.description: Unshaded two-set Venn diagram. H denotes history and G geography. Parenthesised numbers denote region counts.
spec.mathematics: History only 22; both 20; geography only 10; neither 13; total 65.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no completed diagram appears in the student prompt.

answer.worked:
Let $H$ denote history and $G$ geography. The Venn diagram has $42-20=22$ in history only, $30-20=10$ in geography only, and $20$ in both.

$$\begin{align*}P(H\cup G)&=\frac{22+20+10}{65}\\P(H\cup G)&=\frac{52}{65}\\P(H\cup G)&=\frac45\end{align*}$$

The union contains $22+20+10=52$ students, so $65-52=13$ study neither subject.

$$\begin{align*}P(H^c\cap G^c)&=\frac{13}{65}\\P(H^c\cap G^c)&=\frac15\end{align*}$$

The history-only region contains $42-20=22$ students.

$$P(H\cap G^c)=\frac{22}{65}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: only one of history or geography

answer.worked:
The history-only and geography-only regions contain $22$ and $10$ students. These regions are mutually exclusive.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{exactly one subject})&=\frac{22+10}{65}\\P(\text{exactly one subject})&=\frac{32}{65}\end{align*}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: Example 5 on PDF page 8 places the intersection count first, subtracts it from each subject total to obtain the exclusive regions, and uses the remaining count outside both sets. Probabilities are favourable region counts divided by the total; exactly one combines the two mutually exclusive outer regions.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Question 11 directly applies Example 5 to subject enrolments, assessing union, complement, history only and exactly one through a Venn diagram.
